title: Nvidia trims its OpenAI Ohio backstop from $250B to under $120B after investor pushback
subtitle: The revised guarantee covers only the first phase of the 10-gigawatt Piketon campus, with a separate GPU-financing line of up to $350B being negotiated in parallel — a scale-back that acknowledges how much single-customer risk Nvidia had absorbed.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Nvidia is cutting its financial guarantee for OpenAI's planned Ohio data-center campus from roughly $250 billion to less than $120 billion, according to a Wall Street Journal report picked up by wire services on August 14. The reduced backstop covers only the first phase of the 10-gigawatt build on U.S. Department of Energy land in Pike County, near Piketon. A separate GPU financing arrangement of as much as $350 billion is being negotiated alongside the revised backstop, and the two sides are said to be nearing a signed agreement that could land within days.

The scale-back happened because investors pressed Nvidia over concentration risk. A $250 billion guarantee against a single customer's site would have sat on Nvidia's balance sheet as a contingent obligation larger than most Fortune 500 market caps, and analysts on the Q2 call had already flagged the exposure as the primary reason to model conservative downside cases. Splitting the commitment into a smaller backstop and a bigger, structured GPU-financing line lets Nvidia keep the deal alive without carrying the full first-loss position — the loans get syndicated, the risk gets shared, and the accounting looks less alarming.

The story matters because it is the first visible retreat from the escalating vendor-financing pattern that defined the last twelve months of AI infrastructure. Nvidia, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Broadcom, and the neocloud operators have been stitching together compute deals structured as reciprocal commitments — the chipmaker backstops the data center, the model lab buys the chips, the cloud provider hosts the workload — and each new round has been larger than the last. A public dial-back on the biggest of those knots suggests the market has a limit, even if the appetite for compute does not.

Takeaway for learners: watch the plumbing, not the press releases. When Nvidia and OpenAI announce a signed deal in the coming days, the interesting number will not be the topline — it will be the split between the reduced backstop and the GPU financing line, because that split reveals how much risk each side is actually carrying. In a market where every party claims exponential demand, the terms of the financing tell you which of them is willing to bet their own balance sheet on it.
